title: Is there a transcription model meaningfully better than what we have? — live (PR-83)
question: The 2025 AMT Challenge ranks MIROS 0.5998 and YourMT3-YPTF-MoE-M 0.5938 above an MT3 baseline of 0.3932. Those are their numbers on their audio. This file is ours, on ours.

honesty: Ground truth is exact: the reference notes are the same array handed to the synth, so there is no alignment and no annotator.

Timbre is NOT real. REFERENCE_SYNTH_V1 is band-limited oscillators plus filtered noise; every model measured here was trained on sampled or recorded instruments, so this audio is out of distribution for all of them.
Therefore absolute F1 on this tier is a floor, not a production estimate. What transfers is the RANKING, and only because every model is given the byte-identical WAV (sha256 recorded per clip).
This tier cannot answer 'how good will this be on a user's recording'. Answering that needs real audio with human-verified notes, which this stream did not have and did not fabricate.

metric.offsetRule: later of 50 ms or 20 % of the reference note's duration (mir_eval default; the 2025 AMT Challenge's rule)
metric.instrumentAware: match requires the same drum flag and the same GM family (arrangerRemi.familyOf), not the same GM program number
metric.matching: maximum bipartite matching (Kuhn), as mir_eval.transcription does it

cost.deviceNote: priced at the A10G rate; the container's torch.cuda.get_device_name() reported 'NVIDIA A10' (identity.runtime.gpuName), not 'NVIDIA A10G' as the other two YourMT3 runs did

caveats: Every model was given the byte-identical WAV; the scorer refuses if a worker's reported audio sha256 does not match the gold clip.
SYNTHETIC_EXACT is not real audio. Absolute F1 here is a floor for every model, and the ranking is the transferable part.
Basic Pitch predicts no instrument at all. Its instrument-aware F1 measures a placeholder GM program the adapter assigns, not a prediction; the pitch-only column is its fair number.
Nothing in this file promotes anything. Routing is unchanged.

spend.method: Container wall-clock seconds measured inside the run, priced at Modal's published rates (A10G $0.000306/s; CPU core $0.0000131/core/s, 4 cores). Computed, not read off an invoice. Image builds are additional and are accounted separately below.

overheadNotMeasuredPerModel.imageBuilds: 9 builds across 3 worker services (5 yourmt3, 4 mt3-baseline). Mostly CPU build containers; two yourmt3 builds ran a GPU smoke on A10G (~3 min each).
overheadNotMeasuredPerModel.contaminatedRun: The first yourmt3 sweep spent ~343 s of A10G on YPTF+Single (12 load failures) and YMT3+ (12 clips at 0 notes) before the config-leak guard existed. ~$0.10, and it bought the diagnosis.
overheadNotMeasuredPerModel.estimatedTotalUsd: well under the $25 ceiling; the authoritative figure is the Modal dashboard for workspace windot100

spend.invoice: not read; computed from measured seconds. The authoritative figure is the Modal dashboard for workspace windot100.

runs.what: first sweep: three variants looped in ONE container, before the config-leak guard existed
runs.scored: YPTF.MoE+Multi only (built first, so its config was clean; 47.1M parameters)

dropped.error: size mismatch for encoder.latent_array.latents: checkpoint [24, 128], current model [26, 128] (the leaked -nl 26 from YPTF.MoE+Multi)

dropped.outcome: loaded silently under the leaked config (strict=False) at 47.1M parameters — 45.7M when built clean — and returned 0 notes on all 12 clips; NOT scored

runs.diagnosis: upstream model.init_train.update_config mutates a module-level model_cfg; ymt3_infer.load_model now refuses a second variant per process and modal_app.sweep fans out one container per variant

runs.what: second sweep: one container per variant

dropped.outcome: the guard fired on all 12 clips: Modal reused the warm YPTF+Single container for the second .remote() call, so the refusal is the guard working, not a model failure

runs.what: third sweep: YMT3+ alone in its own invocation (45.7M parameters)
fourth and last MT3 image build attempt (--no-build-isolation): crepe built, tflite-support failed for want of pybind11; ImageBuildError
runs.note: the Dockerfile pins both checkpoint sha256s from the HF LFS pointers and checks them, but no MT3 image ever built, so nothing was verified in a container
